newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain BBV capital restructuring approved.
newsitem.headline: Spain BBV capital restructuring approved.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) said on Thursday its shareholders had approved changes in its capital structure at an extraordinary meeting.
"In the extraordinary meeting...shareholders approved capital measures designed to optimise the management of the banks equity and maximise its earnings per share," BBV said in a statement.

1: Nominal share value will be reduced on July 19 by 25 pesetas to 550 pesetas from 575 as already agreed at a February 22 shareholder meeting. The 25 pesetas would be paid back to shareholders, who will cash in a net value of 24.75 pesetas/share.

2. Immediately thereafter BBV will raise its capital to 51.69 billion pesetas, charged to reserves. With that, the share nominal will be increased to 780 pesetas from 550. In this way, the shareholder benefits from part of accumulated reserves.

3. Finally, and simultaneously with the above, the number of shares in circulation will be multiplied by three, resulting in equity capital represented by 674.19 million shares with a nominal value of 260 pesetas per share.
In addition, BBV will cancel one percent, or 6,741,900 shares, from its treasury stock.
